# MM-P3-L2-HT03 - Maintenance manual - Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P3, line P3-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L2-HT03

Scope
This manual describes the preventive and corrective maintenance required to maintain safe, repeatable heat treat cycles for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03). The content focuses on the furnace systems that affect metallurgical outcomes: atmosphere control, heating elements, thermocouple integrity, door seals, and the control system. The austenitizing setpoint for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03) is 870 °C. The thermocouple calibration interval for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03) is 55 days. Use this document as the controlled reference for maintenance planning, execution, and record keeping. For procedural details on safe lockout and tagout, reference SOP-P3-L2-01. For shipping and spares bulletins, reference SB-1015 and SB-1041.

Tools and consumables
Required tools are those commonly used for furnace maintenance and instrumentation work, including calibrated handheld thermometry, insulation handling tools, soft nonmetallic scrapers, and instrumentation hand tools appropriate for the control vendor. Consumables include replacement thermocouples matched to the control system, replacement door seals compatible with the furnace design, high temperature gasket cement manufacturer recommended for this furnace, and cleaning solvents approved in plant procedures. Ensure all tools and consumables are approved by maintenance supervision and are traceable in stores.

Background and rationale
Maintaining the austenitizing setpoint and thermocouple accuracy directly affects microstructure, mechanical properties, and scrap rates for ring rolling feedstock. The specified austenitizing setpoint ensures full austenitization of the chosen steel grades while minimizing excessive grain growth. Thermocouple drift over time can produce significant process variation; the stated calibration interval is set to balance downtime and process control risk. The maintenance actions in this manual are designed to detect and correct common failure modes that lead to setpoint deviation or thermal nonuniformity.

Procedure
Preliminary steps
Confirm control system alarms are acknowledged and logged prior to work. Isolate power and follow the lockout procedure in SOP-P3-L2-01. Verify the furnace chamber is at ambient conditions before removing insulation or accessing internal components.

Inspection of heating elements and insulation
Visually inspect heating elements for breaks, deformation, or discoloration indicative of overheating. Inspect insulation modules for compression, bridging, or contamination from scale or quench residue. Remove loose debris with nonmetallic tools and vacuum with approved high temperature vacuum equipment. Replace insulation modules showing loss of shape or breaches in the compressive face. When reinstalling insulation, seat modules to prevent hot spots at element supports.

Door seal and mechanical system
Inspect the door seal for continuity, tears, or separation from the backing. Clean mating surfaces and apply approved gasket cement where minor gaps are present. If the seal shows material breakdown or there is evidence of gas leakage during a heat cycle, install the replacement seal per vendor guidance. Verify door hinge and latch function and that door closes uniformly. Adjustments should be made to ensure an even contact surface between the door seal and furnace face.

Thermocouple inspection and calibration
Inspect thermocouple leads and junctions for mechanical damage, abrasions, or loose fittings at process connections. Replace any thermocouple showing physical damage. The thermocouple calibration interval for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P3-L2-HT03) is 55 days; schedule calibration events in maintenance planning to ensure continuity of control accuracy. During calibration, perform a comparison against a laboratory reference standard following the control vendor procedure and record the correction factors. If a thermocouple shows deviation beyond the vendor tolerance, replace it and document the replacement.

Control system and atmosphere control
Verify control loops for heating zones are responding and that setpoint tracking is within expected behavior. Confirm atmosphere supply and return lines are free of obstructions and that purge cycles operate per process requirements. Inspect atmosphere generator components and filtration per SB-1015 guidance for spares and replacement items. Log any variances and tag components for corrective action.

Corrective repairs
For element failure, replace elements using the manufacturer specified replacement items. For insulation breaches, replace affected modules. For control card failures, refer to SB-1041 for spare card handling and vendor contact information. After any corrective repair, perform a controlled heat cycle using an empty load to validate uniformity and control accuracy before returning the furnace to production.

Acceptance criteria
Successful completion of maintenance is confirmed when the following conditions are met:
- Control maintains the austenitizing setpoint within the control system limits established by the furnace vendor and process engineering.
- Thermocouples read consistently with the laboratory reference within the vendor tolerance after calibration.
- Door seal provides no measurable leakage during a monitored purge or heat cycle.
- Visual inspection reveals no degraded insulation or compromised heating elements.

Records to keep
Maintain a maintenance log for EQ-P3-L2-HT03 that includes a description of work performed, parts replaced, serial numbers where applicable, and the name of the technician and supervisor who authorized the action. Log thermocouple calibration results and any correction factors applied to control settings. Retain pre- and post-maintenance furnace temperature profile captures for each validation run. File all entries in the document control system and link maintenance records to the equipment history as required.

Examples and notes
Example maintenance entries should document the observed condition, corrective action, parts used, and references to the related documents SB-1015, SB-1041, and SOP-P3-L2-01. When scheduling thermocouple calibration events, align planned outage windows with production planning. If recurring deviations are observed after repeated maintenance, escalate to process engineering for metallurgical investigation.

References
SB-1015  
SB-1041  
SOP-P3-L2-01

Revision history and approvals are maintained in the document control system associated with this manual.
